stories.headline: Odisha worker allegedly forced into Russia-Ukraine war, family seeks rescue
stories.title: Odisha worker allegedly forced into Russia-Ukraine war, family seeks rescue
stories.summary: Maguni Sahu’s family alleges that agents duped the 35-year-old migrant worker from Ganjam into working for an armed organisation somewhere along the Russia-Ukraine border, and says it has been out of touch with him for five days
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: A migrant worker from Odisha’s Ganjam district was allegedly duped by agents and forced to work for an armed organisation in Russia, his family members said.
Identified as Maguni Sahu, 35, the worker had travelled to Russia about four months ago to work at an apple farm in Krasnodar.

A resident of Mathura village under Khallikote block in Ganjam district, Mr. Sahu had worked at the farm for barely a month before he was allegedly deceived into working for an organisation believed to be linked to the Russian military.
“My maternal uncle, Maguni Sahu, was deceived by some agents in Russia.
He has studied only up to Class X. He informed us that he was forced to work for an armed organisation, though he could not identify it.
The only thing he could figure out was that he was working somewhere along the Russia-Ukraine border,” said his nephew, Deepak Pradhan, on Saturday (November 28, 2026).
Mr. Sahu’s family members have approached the Ganjam Collector and labour officials, seeking their intervention to secure his release and facilitate his return to India.
However, their efforts have so far yielded no results.
“We have not been able to contact my uncle for the past five days,” Mr. Pradhan said.
“However, after reaching Russia and joining the apple factory, my son reportedly received only around Rs.
40,000 per month, contrary to the salary and employment conditions promised during recruitment,” his father stated in the letter.
He further alleged that during this difficult period, another Indian worker from Bihar assured his son of a better-paying opportunity, offering a monthly salary of ₹1.2 lakh or more.

stories.headline: Delimitation in India’s strategic periphery: a national security blind spot
stories.title: Delimitation in India’s strategic periphery: a national security blind spot
stories.summary: The old Jammu-Poonch constituency was never the preserve of a single political formation
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in title weight 70
article_sentences: The debate over delimitation in India is generally framed around equal representation and changing population patterns.
Yet, in strategically sensitive regions, redrawing electoral boundaries has implications that extend well beyond electoral arithmetic.

As Parliament considers a fresh delimitation initiative, Jammu and Kashmir offers an important case study of how constituency restructuring can reshape political geography, regional relationships and, ultimately, the strategic considerations underpinning national security.

While the delimitation of individual Assembly constituencies in Jammu and Kashmir and Assam attracted considerable public and political attention in 2022–23, far less scrutiny was devoted to the restructuring of the Anantnag and Jammu-Poonch Lok Sabha constituencies.

The exercise redrew the parliamentary map by detaching Rajouri and Poonch from the Jammu-Poonch constituency and merging them with the Anantnag constituency in South Kashmir, creating a new geographical and political configuration with wider strategic implications.
On face value, this appeared to be a technical rearrangement of parliamentary representation.
Yet, its impact is extensive.

They need to be examined in greater depth, not merely as an exercise in constituency reorganisation but in terms of their wider and longer-term implications for political representation, regional relationships, social cohesion and national security.
The scale of these implications makes a granular assessment essential.

The restructuring has been criticised for creating conditions conducive to a consolidation of Hindu political representation in Jammu, with the BJP frequently identified as its potential electoral beneficiary.
One may set aside the partisan implications of the exercise, but the very fact that such a perception has gained currency raises questions about the care with which the exercise was conceived.

In a region as politically sensitive as Jammu and Kashmir, delimitation should not merely withstand scrutiny over its constitutional and administrative rationale; it must also be assessed for its foreseeable impact on political representation, inter-community relationships and the wider security environment.

stories.headline: "850 represents murder of Indian democracy": Rahul Gandhi slams PM Modi, Amit Shah & CEC Gyanesh Kumar over Delimitation Bill
stories.title: "850 represents murder of Indian democracy": Rahul Gandhi slams PM Modi, Amit Shah & CEC Gyanesh Kumar over Delimitation Bill
stories.summary: New Delhi , Nov 28 : Launching an all-out political assault ahead of Monday’s Parliament session, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday branded the Centre’s proposed 850-seat Lok Sabha expansion the "murder of Indian democracy" and a "new escape route" designed to let Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar redraw India’s electoral map at will. Addressing a press conference in the national capital after a strategy huddle of INDIA bloc floor leaders, Gandhi displayed a point-by-point comparison chart contrasting the Centre’s Delimitation and Women’s Reservation package with the Opposition’s counter-demands, calling for women’s quota to be implemented immediately on the existing 543 seats with an OBC sub-quota, a bipartisan Delimitation Commission, and reliance on the 2027 caste census rather than 2011 figures. Directly appealing to young voters, Gandhi alleged that the government was using women’s reservation as a pretext to engineer massive gerrymandering on the lines of Assam and Jammu and Kashmir. "Their belief is that the Lok Sabha, instead of having 543 members, should have 850 members, and they use this excuse of women's reservation. The women's reservation bill has already been passed. It can be implemented tomorrow. So the question is, why 850? The answer lies in Assam, and it lies in Jammu and Kashmir because when you have 850 seats to play with, the amount of changes that you can make, the amount of redesigning that you can do to the electoral map of India is massive. So this gives the BJP space to redraw India's electoral map to its advantage, will allow them to weaken the representation of communities who are opposed to them, and allows them to target specific opposition leaders," Gandhi said. Targeting the structure of the proposed Delimitation Commission, he accused the ruling dispensation of capturing the panel. "Gen Z, please remember this number. This number represents the murder of Indian democracy, 850. The idea is to give Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, and Gyanesh Kumar a blank canvas to redesign India's constituency map however they feel like. Gen Z, remember this: this exact thing is going to happen to the map of India so that these criminal thieves can continue to steal from this country and destroy your future. Here is the Delimitation Commission: you can see Gyanesh Kumar will be a member, along with one former Supreme Court judge selected by Modi and Shah and guess who chooses the third member? Mr Gyanesh Kumar himself chooses the third member of the committee, while the first member is chosen by Modi and Shah. Gyanesh Kumar has overseen the destruction of the democratic system, and he is now going to oversee the destruction of this country. The EC has been captured. Now, the Delimitation Commission is being operationalised to do this. The composition of the delimitation gives Modi and Shah full control, and Gyanesh's decisions cannot be challenged in court." Accusing the BJP of sidelining the caste census and rendering the upcoming 2027 enumeration irrelevant, Gandhi warned that freezing seat proportions on 2011 Census data until 2051 would deny marginalised communities their rightful share for four decades. "The caste census has been put aside, and the 2027 Census has been rendered irrelevant. Why? Because it is going to show some very inconvenient facts, which the BJP does not appreciate. So they are going to use the 2011 Census, and everything is going to be frozen till 2051. Means for 40 years, you can forget social justice. They're undermining the rights of SC, ST, OBC, disempowering minorities. The share of SC/ST seats will be frozen for 40 years; their population is going to increase, yet their seats are not going to be increased. Obviously, they do not want the outcome of a caste census. We want a bipartisan Delimitation Commission... Women's reservation at 850, and we say at 543 with a sub-quota for OBCs. The question here is giving the BJP a blank slate to reshape the foundations of Indian democracy," he stated. Linking the delimitation push to his recurring allegations of electoral manipulation in 2024, Gandhi claimed the youth had cornered the ruling party on "vote chori" (vote theft) and warned of imminent disclosures against the CEC. "They have captured the EVM. They've captured the voting process. Now they want to destroy the entire constituency structure. We are not going to allow the BJP to convert this country into a dictatorship. It is not going to happen. The 2024 election was a fake election... We, the youth of the country and Gen Z, have cornered the BJP on the issue of vote chori. We closed their path and shut that door; now they have come up with a new plan and are trying to open a new route," Gandhi said. "The idea that they can rig elections wherever they want, whenever they want, is an idea whose time is gone. They can still rig elections, but India knows that they are rigging them. Our polling shows us that 80% of India and almost 100% of Gen Z believe that Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, and Gyanesh Kumar steal elections. Now, they have come out with a new plan," he added. Citing alleged irregularities across states, Gandhi concluded with a direct warning to the CEC. "Today I want to explain to you what this new escape route looks like, what the design is, and what the outcome is going to be...EC itself has said 140 million people voted in 2024 who should not have voted in 2024, who were not eligible voters. That means, according to the EC itself, the 2024 election was illegal. In Jammu and Kashmir, seats were redrawn; in Bihar, we have shown you voter deletion; in Assam, restructuring the entire state to suit the BJP; in West Bengal, 100-plus seats stolen...We have trapped Modi, Shah, and Gyanesh. They know it, we know it. And as I have told you, we have enough information on Mr Gyanesh Kumar, and he is not going to escape. We are going to be releasing that information to you soon..." The Union Cabinet has cleared three revised draft legislations, including the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, and a proposed amendment to Union Territories laws. The Bills are scheduled to be taken up during the special session of Parliament beginning November 30. The Opposition has supported women's reservation but objected to linking its implementation with delimitation. It has also demanded that the exercise be based on the latest Census data. The Centre has proposed using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies and determining SC/ST-reserved seats, while retaining the 1971 population basis for state-wise allocation of Lok Sabha seats until 2051. (ANI)

stories.headline: Delimitation bill says EC to redraw seats in Pakistan-held J&K once occupation ends
stories.title: Delimitation bill says EC to redraw seats in Pakistan-held J&K once occupation ends
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 28: A bill listed for introduction in the Lok Sabha makes advance provision for redrawing constituencies in the part of Jammu and Kashmir under Pakistan's occupation, to take effect once the occupation ends. Section 3(4) of the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026 says the Election Commission would act as the Delimitation Commission for the J&K Assembly constituencies in that area "when the area... ceases to be so occupied." The clause is conditional. The bill uses the phrase "falling under the occupation of Pakistan" and does not use the term "PoK." The Election Commission itself would act as the Delimitation Commission for this area. Elsewhere, the bill sets up a separate commission chaired by a sitting or retired Supreme Court judge, with the Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner and the State Election Commissioner as members. The clause is limited to the J&K Legislative Assembly. It does not mention Lok Sabha seats for the area. The bill does not mention the 24 Assembly seats long reserved for the area, and does not say whether its 50 per cent seat increase would apply there. Separately, the government will also introduce the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Second Bill, 2026, which seeks to amend three laws of Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry to align them with the proposed 132nd Constitutional Amendment, which would implement women's reservation after a fresh delimitation with a 50 per cent increase in seats. Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir and Puducherry are the three Union territories with legislative assemblies. The bills on delimitation and UTs were earlier introduced in April along with the Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill to operationalise the women's quota from 2029. Since the Constitution amendment bill failed to pass through in the Lok Sabha due to lack of numbers, the other two could not come up for voting. Now, the pending two will be withdrawn, and fresh ones will be introduced on Monday along with the new constitution amendment bill.

stories.headline: Rajnath Singh tells Congress to ‘pack up’, questions ‘vote theft’ allegations
stories.title: Rajnath Singh tells Congress to ‘pack up’, questions ‘vote theft’ allegations
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 28 : Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday hit out at the Congress over its ‘vote theft’ allegations, challenging the opposition party to produce evidence of electoral malpractice and declaring, “Modi ji is not going anywhere. It is time for Congress to pack up.” Defending the abrogation of Article 370, Singh said the decision had accelerated development in Jammu and Kashmir and weakened terrorism and separatism in the region. Addressing the BJP’s ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ rally at Parade Ground in Jammu, Singh, as per the news agency—Kashmir News Observer (KNO), said a healthy democracy required respect for the people’s mandate and democratic institutions. He hit out at the Congress for blaming the electoral process for its repeated election defeats instead of introspecting on its own performance. “Give me at least one proof. Where has the vote been stolen?” he asked, challenging the opposition to substantiate its allegations. Referring to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s remarks on alleged electoral irregularities, Singh questioned how such allegations could be repeatedly levelled without supporting evidence. He also referred to the appointment of an Election Commissioner in 2014 during the Congress-led government, arguing that the BJP could not be held responsible for the appointment. Singh said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had become Prime Minister through the people’s mandate and that only the people of India had the authority to take that mandate away. He maintained that the BJP pursued politics for nation-building rather than merely capturing power, adding that the party would oppose any attempt to undermine the country’s democratic institutions. Turning to Jammu and Kashmir, Singh described the Union Territory as India’s “crown jewel” and recalled the contributions of Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee and Pandit Prem Nath Dogra towards its integration with the country. Recalling Mukherjee’s slogan of “one country, one constitution and one symbol”, he said several people from Jammu and Kashmir had sacrificed their lives for the country’s unity and integrity. Singh said the abrogation of Article 370 in August 2019 fulfilled the BJP’s long-standing commitment and extended several rights to the people of Jammu and Kashmir that, according to him, had previously been denied to them. He said that Article 370 had contributed to the growth of terrorism and said its removal had helped weaken terrorism and separatist forces in the region. Referring to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s approach towards Kashmir, Singh invoked the principles of humanity, democracy and Kashmiriyat, saying the region needed to look towards the future rather than remain confined to the past. “After Article 370, no power in the world can stop Jammu and Kashmir from becoming a developed state of India,” he said. Highlighting the development initiatives undertaken by the Centre, Singh referred to the expansion of healthcare infrastructure, including AIIMS facilities in Jammu and Kashmir, and said people no longer needed to travel to Delhi for treatment of several major ailments. He also cited tourism figures to underline the region’s growing popularity, stating that 4.76 crore tourists visited Jammu and Kashmir during 2017–20, compared to 7.85 crore during 2023–25. He said the increase in tourist arrivals was benefiting local businesses, with visitors spending money on goods and services and contributing to the regional economy. Singh asserted that Jammu and Kashmir had witnessed rapid development under the Modi-led government and was now receiving its due rights and opportunities. The Defence Minister also criticised the Congress over its past record, citing the Emergency and the Shah Bano case as examples of what he described as the party’s disregard for democratic and constitutional principles. He said the Congress government had overturned the Supreme Court’s decision in the Shah Bano case to appease certain sections and referred to the dismissal of elected governments in different states during Congress rule. Singh said opposing a government and opposing the country were two different things, accusing the Congress leadership of failing to maintain that distinction. He also criticised Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on national security and religious issues, referring to his statements concerning Indian soldiers and China, as well as his comments on Hindu identity and the Ram temple. On Parliament, Singh said issues concerning the country should be debated in the House, while alleging that Rahul Gandhi’s attendance was below the national average for MPs and that he remained more focused on opposing Modi than raising public issues. Singh said the Prime Minister had earned people’s trust through his work and commitment, adding that political power could neither be treated as anyone’s birthright nor inherited. Calling upon people to safeguard India’s unity, integrity, Constitution and democratic institutions, the Defence Minister said protecting these values required a collective commitment.—(KNO)

opening: Jammu, Nov 28: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday hit out at the Congress over its ‘vote theft’ allegations, challenging the opposition party to produce evidence of electoral malpractice and declaring, “Modi ji is not going anywhere.

It is time for Congress to pack up.” Defending the abrogation of Article 370, Singh said the decision had accelerated development in Jammu and Kashmir and weakened terrorism and separatism in the region.
body: Addressing the BJP’s ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ rally at Parade Ground in Jammu, Singh, as per the news agency—Kashmir News Observer (KNO), said a healthy democracy required respect for the people’s mandate and democratic institutions.
He hit out at the Congress for blaming the electoral process for its repeated election defeats instead of introspecting on its own performance.
“Give me at least one proof.
Where has the vote been stolen?” he asked, challenging the opposition to substantiate its allegations.
Referring to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s remarks on alleged electoral irregularities, Singh questioned how such allegations could be repeatedly levelled without supporting evidence.
He also referred to the appointment of an Election Commissioner in 2014 during the Congress-led government, arguing that the BJP could not be held responsible for the appointment.
Singh said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had become Prime Minister through the people’s mandate and that only the people of India had the authority to take that mandate away.
He maintained that the BJP pursued politics for nation-building rather than merely capturing power, adding that the party would oppose any attempt to undermine the country’s democratic institutions.

Turning to Jammu and Kashmir, Singh described the Union Territory as India’s “crown jewel” and recalled the contributions of Dr Shyama Prasad Mukherjee and Pandit Prem Nath Dogra towards its integration with the country.
Recalling Mukherjee’s slogan of “one country, one constitution and one symbol”, he said several people from Jammu and Kashmir had sacrificed their lives for the country’s unity and integrity.

Singh said the abrogation of Article 370 in August 2019 fulfilled the BJP’s long-standing commitment and extended several rights to the people of Jammu and Kashmir that, according to him, had previously been denied to them.
He said that Article 370 had contributed to the growth of terrorism and said its removal had helped weaken terrorism and separatist forces in the region.

Referring to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s approach towards Kashmir, Singh invoked the principles of humanity, democracy and Kashmiriyat, saying the region needed to look towards the future rather than remain confined to the past.
“After Article 370, no power in the world can stop Jammu and Kashmir from becoming a developed state of India,” he said.

Highlighting the development initiatives undertaken by the Centre, Singh referred to the expansion of healthcare infrastructure, including AIIMS facilities in Jammu and Kashmir, and said people no longer needed to travel to Delhi for treatment of several major ailments.
He also cited tourism figures to underline the region’s growing popularity, stating that 4.76 crore tourists visited Jammu and Kashmir during 2017–20, compared to 7.85 crore during 2023–25.
He said the increase in tourist arrivals was benefiting local businesses, with visitors spending money on goods and services and contributing to the regional economy.
Singh asserted that Jammu and Kashmir had witnessed rapid development under the Modi-led government and was now receiving its due rights and opportunities.

The Defence Minister also criticised the Congress over its past record, citing the Emergency and the Shah Bano case as examples of what he described as the party’s disregard for democratic and constitutional principles.

He said the Congress government had overturned the Supreme Court’s decision in the Shah Bano case to appease certain sections and referred to the dismissal of elected governments in different states during Congress rule.
Singh said opposing a government and opposing the country were two different things, accusing the Congress leadership of failing to maintain that distinction.

He also criticised Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on national security and religious issues, referring to his statements concerning Indian soldiers and China, as well as his comments on Hindu identity and the Ram temple.

On Parliament, Singh said issues concerning the country should be debated in the House, while alleging that Rahul Gandhi’s attendance was below the national average for MPs and that he remained more focused on opposing Modi than raising public issues.
Singh said the Prime Minister had earned people’s trust through his work and commitment, adding that political power could neither be treated as anyone’s birthright nor inherited.
Calling upon people to safeguard India’s unity, integrity, Constitution and democratic institutions, the Defence Minister said protecting these values required a collective commitment.—(KNO).

stories.summary: Former Chief Justice of India D Y Chandrachud on Saturday said artificial intelligence can help courts with dull and routine tasks but stressed that the decision and the reasons for it must remain the responsibility of the judge. Speaking at an event on 'AI for all: AI governance and trust, the case for judicial access and an empowered India', he said a human being must decide and sign every judgment. stories.headline: Post 370, J&K witnessing decline in Congress legacy of terrorism, separatism: Rajnath Singh
stories.title: Post 370, J&K witnessing decline in Congress legacy of terrorism, separatism: Rajnath Singh
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 28: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday asserted that J&K, post Article 370, under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, was witnessing gradual end of terrorism and separatism in Kashmir with the diminishing secessionist eco-system, all inherited as Congress legacy. Quoting a Kashmiri adage, Singh stated that for J&K, it was the time to forget the past; look and march forward towards a bright future, awaiting it and none would stop it from becoming a developed state. Singh was addressing a massive public rally at Parade, after leading “Mahapadyatra” (foot-march) with a tricolour in his hands, joined by a large number of J&K party leaders and workers, carrying national flag and party flag amid slogans. The rally was part of BJP’s nationwide campaign “Loktantra Bachao, Arajakata Hatao”. In a tirade against the Congress, the Defence Minister accused it of making futile attempts for “regime change” through anarchy and fake narratives, in league with its allies. He asserted that the accession of J&K with India was not the question of integrating a region but it was a resolve to safeguard and keep intact the soul of India, self-esteem and its integrity. He quoted from the book of a former DGP of J&K to substantiate his point that Article 370 - a Congress legacy was used to promote discriminatory and separatist tendencies in the erstwhile state. “Even a President of India was declared a non-state subject here,” Singh recalled and maintained that PM Modi, realising the vision of Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee and the former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, abrogated Article 370 to undo those tendencies. He said that the history of Jammu was delineated by valour, self-respect and sacrifice. “This land is the abode of the Goddess Vaishno Devi. I pay my obeisance to the Goddess. In BJP’s political journey, J&K has a very special significance as this is the land where Sher-e-Duggar Prem Nath Dogra struggled throughout his life for its (J&K’s) complete integration with India. From this land, the party ideologue Dr Syama Prasad Mookerjee had raised the slogan of “Ek Desh, Ek Vidhan, Ek Nishan” and sacrificed his life for achieving this objective,” Singh maintained. He asserted that a large number of people from J&K laid down their lives for safeguarding the integrity and sovereignty of the country and extended his heartfelt gratitude to them . “J&K is the crown-jewel of India thus for us (BJP), the accession of J&K with India, was not the question of a region but it was a resolve to safeguard and keep intact the soul of India, self-esteem and its integrity. Today, when we’ve formed a government under the leadership of the Prime Minister, one cannot deny the fact that J&K is witnessing inclusive development all across and is marching ahead along with the rest of the country. J&K is getting all its due rights,” he maintained. Regarding Congress, he reiterated that it had reached its “expiry date” and people of India would ensure that it should not come back. “Need of the hour is to take a resolve against all those who were trying to undermine democracy by launching an assault against constitutional institutions as those anarchist forces were not able to win the trust of people and win power,” Singh said. “Congress and its allies are using all ways and means to effect regime change through anarchy but the people of India, who believed in democratic values, would never accept it. Recently in Hyderabad, Congress convened a summit chaired by its top leadership, when an Italian person raised a slogan “Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod.” Congress should remember that the Prime Minister would not leave anywhere but it (Congress) would have to as it left only a legacy of poverty, backwardness, corruption, naxalism and terrorism,” Singh said. He maintained that Congress lost three Lok Sabha elections and numerous assembly elections but unable to digest its defeat or rectify its lacunae, it was blaming constitutional institutions. “Repeatedly it has failed in the examination but instead of rectifying its shortcomings, it is finding solace in absurd excuses, peddling fake narratives and promoting anarchy. In 2014, the Chief Election Commissioner was appointed by the Congress government and not by the BJP, which won a massive public mandate,” the Defence Minister maintained. Taking a dig at the Leader of Opposition (LoP) in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, Singh said, “When Congress is asked to give evidence in support of its “vote Chori” claims, he (Rahul) says - I cannot give any evidence but I’m feeling it. It’s so absurd. One can have a “feeling” of becoming even the US President but that “feeling” will not actually help anyone to acquire that status.” J&K BJP president Sat Sharma, party MPs Jugal Kishore Sharma, Gulam Ali Khatana, former Deputy Chief Minister Dr Nirmal Singh, former J&K BJP president Ravinder Raina and party MLAs shared the dais with the Defence Minister. Sat Sharma, in his welcome address, extended his gratitude to the Defence Minister for accepting the request of J&K BJP unit and sparing his precious time, out of his pre-scheduled programme, to lead “Maha Padyatra” in Jammu. Earlier, the Defence Minister was received and welcomed by the Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha at Jammu airport on his arrival in the winter capital of J&K. At the very outset of his address, Rajnath stated that he was overwhelmed by the tumultuous welcome received in Jammu. Layered security was in place for “Mahapadyatra” and subsequent public rally all across Jammu..

stories.title: Supreme Court refuses to entertain plea to reduce minimum age for contesting elections

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Saturday (November 28, 2026) refused to entertain a plea seeking to reduce the minimum age for contesting parliamentary and state legislature elections.

The counsel appearing for the petitioner told a bench comprising Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh that while the voting age was reduced from 21 to 18, the minimum age to be a member of the Lok Sabha is 25 and 30 for the Rajya Sabha.
The counsel also referred to the minimum age to be a member of the state legislative assembly and state legislative council.
"In this petition, there is a small but very vital issue.
The voting age, by the (Constitution) sixty-first amendment, was reduced from 21 to 18," the counsel said.
When the bench observed that it was not an appropriate petition, the counsel said, "The respondent can just inform the petitioner what is the outcome of his representation."
"For that, you go to the high court under (Article) 226 for getting a direction for deciding your representation," the bench said.
The plea had made the Centre and the Election Commission as party respondents.
The counsel then said that he would like to withdraw his plea.
"Dismissed as withdrawn," the bench said.

stories.headline: Tata Trusts row: Tata Sons moves Bombay High Court, Supreme Court with caveats ahead of meeting
stories.title: Tata Trusts row: Tata Sons moves Bombay High Court, Supreme Court with caveats ahead of meeting
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Tata Sons, the principal holding company of the Tata group, has filed caveats before the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court in connection with the interim order passed by the Bombay High Court on November 27.

The move comes amid speculation that Tata Trusts, which hold 66 per cent stake in Tata Sons, may challenge the single-judge order before a division bench of the Bombay High Court or the Supreme Court.
The caveats were filed late on November 27 and cover proceedings before both the division bench of the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court, legal sources said.
A caveat is filed to ensure that a party is given an opportunity to be heard before a court passes any order on a petition or application filed by the opposing party.
The single bench of the Bombay High Court on Friday refused to grant any interim relief to the trusts, allowing the Tata Sons board meeting, scheduled for November 30, to go ahead.
However, any resolutions passed at the meeting will remain subject to the outcome of the proceedings before the court, which fixed January 21, 2027, as the next date of hearing.
“We are not granting any relief today.

Let the meeting go on as scheduled and everything will be subject to the outcome,” Justice Abhay Ahuja said, making it clear that decisions taken by the Tata Sons board would be subject to further orders of the court.

The Tata group battle on Thursday moved to the Bombay High Court, with Tata Trusts seeking to challenge the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for another five-year term through the casting vote, alleging that the resolution passed by the company’s board on September 17 was ultra vires its Articles of Association and therefore null and void.

Tata Trusts maintained that the reappointment resolution based on the casting vote of the chairman of board meeting – Harish Manwani — was legally invalid because the Articles of Association require the affirmative vote of a majority of the Trusts’ nominee directors for a decision on the appointment or reappointment of the chairman.
Noel Tata voted against the resolution, while Venu Srinivasan supported it.

The trusts sought interim orders restraining Tata Sons and its directors from acting upon the resolution and from passing board resolutions over the objection of either of the two Trust-nominated directors where the affirmative vote of a majority of Trust directors is required.

stories.headline: 13-member panel to light Tirupparankundram lamp at 5 pm in Tamil Nadu
stories.title: 13-member panel to light Tirupparankundram lamp at 5 pm in Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: Madurai (Tamil Nadu), Nov 28 : A 13-member steering committee comprising retired judges, senior administrative officials, security personnel, and temple priests will oversee the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon atop the Tirupparankundram Murugan temple hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai district at 5 p.m. on Saturday, in accordance with the Supreme Court’s directive. The committee includes retired judges Vaidyanathan and Parthiban, Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna, the City Police Commissioner, the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) Inspector General and temple priests. Elaborate security arrangements have been put in place across Tirupparankundram and its surrounding areas, with an additional 400 CRPF personnel arriving to ensure the smooth conduct of the religious ceremony. Central security personnel have been conducting extensive searches on the hill and in adjoining areas as part of precautionary measures. Police deployment has also been strengthened in view of the anticipated influx of devotees. Earlier in the day, retired judges Vaidyanathan and Parthiban, appointed to facilitate the implementation of the Supreme Court’s order, visited the Tirupparankundram Murugan temple and offered prayers. Following special rituals at the temple, the retired judges proceeded towards the hilltop carrying the ceremonial lamp as preparations for the lighting ceremony were completed. The judges also held consultations with the hereditary temple priests, who traditionally perform religious rituals at the Murugan temple. The Madurai District Collector, District Superintendent of Police and other senior officials participated in the discussions. Meanwhile, devotees began gathering at Tirupparankundram from the early hours of Saturday, with authorities expecting a substantial turnout for the much-awaited ceremony. The Health Department has deployed 16 medical teams, including eight mobile medical units, to provide emergency assistance to devotees. Four motorcycle-based medical teams have also been stationed to facilitate rapid access to congested areas, while eight ambulances have been kept on standby to transport patients requiring emergency treatment. Authorities have advised elderly people, children, pregnant women and those suffering from cardiac ailments to refrain from climbing the hill as a precautionary measure. Tirupparankundram, regarded as the first of the six sacred abodes of Lord Murugan, has been at the centre of a prolonged legal controversy over the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the hilltop stone pillar. Saturday’s ceremony assumes significance following the Supreme Court’s intervention, with the administration focusing on ensuring compliance with the judicial directive while maintaining public order and communal harmony. ( IANS)

opening: Madurai (Tamil Nadu), Nov 28: A 13-member steering committee comprising retired judges, senior administrative officials, security personnel, and temple priests will oversee the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon atop the Tirupparankundram Murugan temple hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai district at 5 p.m. on Saturday, in accordance with the Supreme Court’s directive.
The committee includes retired judges Vaidyanathan and Parthiban, Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna, the City.
body: Police Commissioner, the Central Reserve.
Police Force (CRPF) Inspector General and temple priests.

Elaborate security arrangements have been put in place across Tirupparankundram and its surrounding areas, with an additional 400 CRPF personnel arriving to ensure the smooth conduct of the religious ceremony.
Central security personnel have been conducting extensive searches on the hill and in adjoining areas as part of precautionary measures.
Police deployment has also been strengthened in view of the anticipated influx of devotees.

Earlier in the day, retired judges Vaidyanathan and Parthiban, appointed to facilitate the implementation of the Supreme Court’s order, visited the Tirupparankundram Murugan temple and offered prayers.
Following special rituals at the temple, the retired judges proceeded towards the hilltop carrying the ceremonial lamp as preparations for the lighting ceremony were completed.
The judges also held consultations with the hereditary temple priests, who traditionally perform religious rituals at the Murugan temple.
The Madurai District Collector, District Superintendent of Police and other senior officials participated in the discussions.
Meanwhile, devotees began gathering at Tirupparankundram from the early hours of Saturday, with authorities expecting a substantial turnout for the much-awaited ceremony.
The Health Department has deployed 16 medical teams, including eight mobile medical units, to provide emergency assistance to devotees.

Four motorcycle-based medical teams have also been stationed to facilitate rapid access to congested areas, while eight ambulances have been kept on standby to transport patients requiring emergency treatment.
Authorities have advised elderly people, children, pregnant women and those suffering from cardiac ailments to refrain from climbing the hill as a precautionary measure.

Tirupparankundram, regarded as the first of the six sacred abodes of Lord Murugan, has been at the centre of a prolonged legal controversy over the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the hilltop stone pillar.

Saturday’s ceremony assumes significance following the Supreme Court’s intervention, with the administration focusing on ensuring compliance with the judicial directive while maintaining public order and communal harmony.
